must_remember: The scalar product of two vectors is given by $A \cdot B = |A||B| \cos(\theta)$ and yields a scalar quantity.
The vector product of two vectors is given by $A \times B = |A||B| \sin(\theta) \hat{n}$ and is anti-commutative ($A \times B = -B \times A$).
Finite rotations do not behave as vectors because they do not obey commutative addition, whereas infinitesimal rotations do.
The vector triple product expands as $A \times (B \times C) = B(A \cdot C) - C(A \cdot B)$.
The scalar triple product $A \cdot (B \times C)$ represents the geometric volume of the parallelepiped formed by vectors $A$, $B$, and $C$.

glossary.meaning: An algebraic operation that takes two equal-length sequences of numbers (usually coordinate vectors) and returns a single number, expressed as $A \cdot B = A_x B_x + A_y B_y + A_z B_z$.
A binary operation on two vectors in a three-dimensional space that results in a vector perpendicular to both operands.
The dot product of one vector with the cross product of two other vectors, denoted by $A \cdot (B \times C)$.
The cross product of a vector with the cross product of two other vectors, denoted by $A \times (B \times C)$.
